frontmatter.title: Open-system simulation
frontmatter.description: A checked amplitude-damping dilation, reduced-state references and explicit environment/readout costs.

children.value: An environment can carry away information and energy, so a reduced system can evolve irreversibly even when the joint circuit is unitary. A dilation makes that interaction explicit; discarding every environment outcome produces the channel. Conditioning on an environment outcome would be a different operation.
This first open-system example implements a finite-time amplitude-damping channel with an actual two-qubit environment dilation. It belongs to the
. Its circuit, reduced state and observables are checked; general interacting Lindblad algorithms remain planned.

adds a noncommuting Hamiltonian with actual first/second-order channel schedules, fresh environments and an independent Liouvillian reference. The absorbing channel on this page remains its separately checked dissipative ingredient.

The channel uses controlled RY and CX, with gate-based input preparation and a zero-input environment. Tests compare the actual gate circuit’s reduced density operator with an independent Kraus reference. The measured exports include resets, input preparation, basis changes and final measurements. Continuous-angle synthesis, physical faults, hardware timing and a general Lindblad simulator are not implemented.

children.value: The environment is traced/discarded for a retained-state output. The measured circuit instead measures both wires and ignores

environment outcome. It never postselects environment zero: conditioning on an environment result would implement a different task. An inverse dilation is not applied, since it would undo the intended system/environment interaction. Each independent trial begins with a freshly reset/prepared environment.

children.value: The actual circuit is evaluated with Qiskit Statevector/DensityMatrix and partial trace; the reference is formed independently with NumPy matrices and the finite-time formulas above. Those matrices are classical checks, not the quantum implementation. This particular finite-time dilation has no time-discretization approximation: with exact angles it realizes the stated one-jump channel. Tests cover four gate-prepared inputs at several times, arbitrary small mixed inputs, zero/full damping, the semigroup composition rule, positivity, trace and X/Y/Z means. They also check a two-system entangled input under the separately generated tensor product of two independent channels. Such bounded checks do not establish a general many-body algorithm or formal proof.

The complete known-input trial explicitly resets system and environment, prepares the named state, applies the dilation and measures both wires. X readout uses H before measurement; Y readout uses S-dagger then H; Z readout uses no basis rotation. The environment is measured in Z and its bit is ignored. Gate counts include these operations and the decomposition of CRY.

children.value: The generator has a separate input-preserving access API for a caller-supplied quantum state. It does not reset that system or claim to prepare arbitrary mixed inputs.

requires named prepared inputs, so a reset cannot silently erase an unknown input. A density matrix supplied to the bounded classical checking routine initializes the simulator; it is not a quantum state-loading algorithm.

children.value: independent trials. The resource ledger repeats the complete trial counts across that proposal. It is

a joint X/Y/Z tomography or multiple-input/time confidence budget. All settings in the numerical comparison would need their own measurement allocations on a device. An illustrative seeded classical draw from ideal circuit probabilities does not establish that confidence bound.

Channel approximation/representation, coherent synthesis, statistical error and physical faults remain separate. The ideal analytic channel has no time-step approximation; continuous-angle synthesis is pending. A 0.05 observable-error proposal allocates 0.01 to channel bias, 0.01 to synthesis bias and 0.03 to sampling. Statistical failure and total physical-fault probability are separately proposed at 0.005 each. Those allocations do not certify a fault-tolerant circuit. The current static shared resource adapter rejects explicit resets, so initialization must be handled separately and disclosed before any physical projection.

For each fixed rate/time, classical coefficient preparation evaluates exp, sqrt and atan2; the resulting coefficients are reused across trials. Its wall time, classical readout processing, physical reset/discard/readout time, routing, error correction and factories are excluded from these logical counts. No physical-resource improvement or hardware performance is claimed.
The circuit-only independent-channel generator scales by adding one system/environment pair per channel. For example:

Generation stops at 32 system plus 32 environment wires. The public dense-check helpers stay at one system plus one environment; larger generator runs are explicitly marked unvalidated. The independent tensor-product family does not implement interacting Lindblad dynamics. General channels, noncommuting generators, higher-dimensional environments and controlled approximation schemes remain planned until their access circuits and error contracts are implemented.
